AMZN.analysts: Buy consensus — average target ~$321-332 (+30-34%) across ~70 analysts. Morgan Stanley raised its target to $350 and named AMZN a top pick (Oct 19), citing AWS acceleration into 2027-28; JPMorgan, BofA and KeyBanc hold Buys at $320-$380.
AMZN.business: The strongest recent print of the group. Q2 2026: revenue $200.6B (+20% YoY, first $200B+ quarter) vs $196.5B consensus; AWS $42.2B, +37% YoY — fastest since 2021; operating income +43%; AWS backlog ~$496B of contracted commitments. FY capex guided to ~$220B; trailing FCF is negative ~$7.6B.
AMZN.buzz: Explicit lag/value framing is common — 'AWS is running at 37% growth and this stock has no business being at $251,' pointing to ~20x trailing earnings vs a ~$324 mean target. Tone: bullish-but-patient, earnings-dependent.
AMZN.dip: The shallowest dip of the group (-13.6% from high; only -0.7% over one month) — mostly sector-level AI-capex/FCF anxiety, including the Oct 22 Nasdaq drop as investors questioned AI data-center financing costs, rather than any Amazon-specific bad news. It rose ~3.9% on Oct 19 on an analyst upgrade.
AMZN.risks: Execution against a $220B capex plan with negative trailing FCF — if Oct 29 shows AWS growth at/below the low end of the 30-35% expectation, or another capex raise, the 'cheap for its growth' case weakens. Part of Q2's huge EPS beat came from non-operating Anthropic revaluation gains, so headline earnings quality is less spectacular than reported.

ASML.analysts: Buy/Moderate Buy consensus — MarketBeat average target $2,079 (+32%); another tally counts 31 Buy + 7 Overweight of 45, consensus $2,138.73. October: Citi reiterated Buy (Oct 15), JPMorgan trimmed to $2,350 keeping Overweight, RBC Outperform $2,100, CFRA Strong Buy $2,602. One outlier downgrade to Sell at $749.
ASML.business: Very strong. Q3 sales +55% YoY, net income more than doubled to EUR 4.96B, EPS beat, gross margin 57.5% vs 55-57% guidance; FY26 outlook raised a third time; demand exceeds planned supply through 2028 with customers asking about 2029-30 orders; EUR 4.1B buyback in Q3.
ASML.buzz: Positive dip framing — coverage led with 'the Q3 beat is real' and a Buy stance on the ADR; retail sentiment described as 'extremely bullish' post-print; the ~$1,560 level near the 200-day average framed as a typical long-term entry zone.
ASML.dip: Oct 14 Q3: record results but revenue narrowly missed the consensus figure, shares -3% overnight and ~14% below the June high; investors also focused on the rising cost of ASML's capacity-expansion plans, plus the broader AI-unwind/rate backdrop (-7.8% that week).
ASML.risks: Premium multiple leaves no room for error; any hyperscaler capex pullback pushes out EUV orders; China/export-control exposure (~20% of business); high beta amplifies AI-trade swings both ways.

AVGO.analysts: Consensus Buy — 52 of 57 analysts rate Buy, 5 Hold, zero Sell. MarketBeat average target $511.88 (+59% vs price); JPMorgan $580, BofA $530, BMO $455.
AVGO.business: Strong and accelerating. Q3 FY26 revenue $29.6B (+86% YoY), AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B (+221% YoY), adjusted EPS +96%, free cash flow $13.7B (46% of revenue). Management guides AI revenue roughly doubling again into FY27 (~$115B) and ~$230B by FY28.
AVGO.buzz: Explicit buy-the-dip framing: TipRanks (Oct 20) — 'Broadcom's Sell-Off Is Starting to Look Like an Overreaction.' Social creators tag it a 'right now' buy on Google/Meta custom-chip demand.
AVGO.dip: Two-stage fall: a September print where Q4 revenue guidance of $34.8B landed a hair under the $35.03B expected (-4-6% on a 0.7% 'miss'), then the October AI-chip rout compounded it (-4.3% on Oct 22 alone, peers averaged -6.1% that week). Now near its 52-week low area.
AVGO.risks: The bar is extreme — a 0.7% guidance shortfall caused a selloff, so any wobble at the Dec 9 print hits hard. ~41x earnings prices in flawless execution; insiders sold $533.7M vs $374K of buys Apr-Oct (often routine/planned, but noted).

BKNG.analysts: TipRanks Strong Buy (22 Buy / 7 Hold), consensus ~$233 (+50%); MarketBeat Moderate Buy, average $233.71. Recent: BTIG Buy $250 (Oct 22), Melius $225 (Oct 20), BofA Buy $234 (Oct 15). Bears: Cantor Fitzgerald cut to $170 Neutral (Oct 12), Wells Fargo $190 'Reduce' (Oct 7).
BKNG.business: Strong and cash-generative. Q2 revenue $7.35B (+8%), adjusted EPS $2.54 (+15%), gross bookings $51B (+9%), adjusted EBITDA $2.65B (+9%), FCF $3.6B (+16%), a record $4.1B returned to shareholders. FY26 consensus still calls for EPS +~15%.
BKNG.buzz: The strongest explicit buy-the-dip framing of the researched names — Motley Fool (Oct 24): 'I would invest in Booking right now… beaten down… this won't last forever.' Insider Monkey argues it is more profitable than Airbnb at half the forward multiple with twice the FCF.
BKNG.dip: A year-long de-rating (-26/27% YTD): Q2 beat followed by soft Q3 guidance (growth of just 4-6%), Middle East conflict hitting long-haul travel and FX, an FTC fees probe into Priceline with a possible ~$500M bill, and the agentic-AI bypass fear — one study found AI tools send 71% of travelers to book direct. Note: a 25-for-1 split completed Apr 2, 2026.
BKNG.risks: AI disintermediation may be structural, not cyclical (direct-booking shift, take-rate pressure); FTC outcome; geopolitics/oil hitting international travel; growth decelerating to mid-single digits.

CAT.analysts: Moderate Buy consensus, average target ~$965-968 (+41%). October cuts kept bullish ratings: Truist $1,100 Buy, Oppenheimer $1,009 Outperform, BofA $850 Buy, JPMorgan/Citi $1,100. Bear outlier: Bernstein $749, Market Perform, on bookings momentum.
CAT.business: Fundamentally record-setting, not deteriorating. Q2 (Aug 4): revenue $20.54B (+23.7% YoY, first $20B+ quarter), adjusted EPS $8.17 vs $6.22 consensus, backlog ~$72B, full-year guidance raised to mid-to-high-teens sales growth.
CAT.buzz: Active dip narrative — multiple outlets flag a hammer pattern and upward estimate revisions as 'a buying opportunity'; Zacks lists CAT among likely Q3 outperformers. Social is split: dip-buying reels vs viral posts hyping Michael Burry's June 30 short position.
CAT.dip: Unwind from a late-June record high ($1,064.90): profit-taking and repricing of its AI/data-center power premium amid an AI-industrials selloff, surging yields (10-year ~5.35%, September Fed hike) and inflation fears — plus a string of analyst target cuts and a ~$600M Q3 tariff burden.
CAT.risks: Bernstein's peak-backlog/weakening-bookings concern, a still-premium ~30x P/E, tariff costs (~$2.2B FY estimate), and whether data-center power demand is durable. Q3 on Oct 29 is the immediate test.

GE.analysts: Strong Buy consensus among 22 analysts, average target $394.14 (+38%) — most recent compilation Sep 30; no notable October downgrades found. One model-based service rates it Hold purely on valuation.
GE.business: Fundamentally strong. Adjusted EPS $2.25 (+36%) vs $2.01 consensus, adjusted revenue $13.3B (+18%), orders $19.0B (+49%, 1.35 book-to-bill), operating profit +30%; FY26 guidance raised (EPS $8.00-8.10, revenue growth 19-20%, FCF $9.1-9.4B); services backlog >$170B.
GE.buzz: Muted vs the chip names — media widely ran 'beat, raised, fell anyway' explainers framing it as a growth-slope repricing rather than a franchise verdict, but no prominent October 'buy the dip' call, and little social-media presence.
GE.dip: Sell-the-news. Q3 (Oct 20) was a beat-and-raise, yet shares fell ~3.7% that day and kept sliding (fourth straight post-earnings drop): Q3 FCF fell 14% YoY to $2.0B, commercial services growth decelerated to ~17% from 32% in H1, LEAP delivery growth slowed to ~5%, GE9X revenue deferred until FAA certification, and the stock was already rich at ~38.7x guided 2026 EPS.
GE.risks: The bear case is 2027 aftermarket deceleration (services growth already halved in H2); casting-supply bottlenecks; GE9X certification timing; margin expansion pushed to 2028; still ~35x earnings, so little margin of safety if the slope disappoints.

GOOGL.analysts: Strong Buy consensus — average target ~$430 (+34%); one tally counts 83 analysts: 72 Buy / 10 Hold / 1 Sell. Wells Fargo raised to $417 (Overweight, Oct 6); JPMorgan $425; BMO Buy $465; Morgan Stanley Buy. Citizens cut its target to $450 but reiterated Buy, flagging AI-agent competition to Search.
GOOGL.business: Strong on last reported numbers. Q2: Google Cloud +82% YoY with a ~$514B backlog; trailing revenue $445.9B (+20%), net income +111%; search sessions +36% YoY; external TPU sales becoming a real revenue line.
GOOGL.buzz: The clearest 'great company on sale' narrative of the group in media/tools coverage — forward PEG ~0.53 cited as undervalued; Cloud framed as the trigger. Buzz is analyst/media-led rather than social-led.
GOOGL.dip: Capex/FCF backlash plus AI-search fear, not weak results. After Q2, investors focused on capex guidance raised to $195-205B for 2026 and Q2 free cash flow of -$5.9B, which outweighed 82% Cloud growth; a $40B at-the-market share offering added supply. Shares slid into the late-October AI-debt selloff.
GOOGL.risks: The Oct 28 print is binary in the wrong week (same day as the Fed decision and Microsoft earnings): a Cloud slowdown, a 2027 capex shock, or Search commentary confirming AI-agent share loss re-rates it lower.

MCD.analysts: Moderate Buy consensus, average target $295.94 (+19%) — but October was a wave of cuts: Bernstein $295->$250 Market Perform, Guggenheim $290->$250 Neutral, Wells Fargo $300->$270 Overweight, KeyCorp $305->$280 Overweight. Lone Sell: Melius at $230.
MCD.business: Slowing but still growing and profitable. Q2 global comps +1.3%, U.S. comps +0.8% (traffic negative, check positive), revenue $7.10B (+3.7%), EPS $3.38 vs $3.32 consensus. The NEXT plan targets low-to-mid-50% operating margin by 2030. Q3 due Nov 4.
MCD.buzz: Very explicit dip coverage — Zacks: 'McDonald's Stock Down 23% in 6 Months: Should Investors Buy the Dip?'; MarketBeat: 'MCD Stock Is Deeply Oversold: Is It Time to Buy the Dip?' (~30% implied upside, 3.2% dividend); TipRanks: 'McDonald's Stock Looks Like a Buy after the Dip.'
MCD.dip: Company-specific U.S. slump — shares -22.9% in six months on weak U.S. comps, a value menu that missed, poor marketing/execution and negative guest counts, plus investor concern over the $8.5B 'McDonald's > NEXT' plan (Sep 23 Investor Day) slowing unit growth and lifting capex.
MCD.risks: U.S. guest counts (especially low-income) haven't stabilized — an affordability headwind management itself acknowledged; GLP-1/wellness trends are a structural overhang; $229 support and the 2022 low (~$217) are must-hold levels, with Nov 4 earnings the decider.

META.analysts: Strong Buy on TipRanks (38 Buy / 6 Hold), average target $828.28 (+29%). Morgan Stanley raised its target to $820 (Overweight, Oct 21-22); Bernstein Buy $800; BofA Buy $810. Cautious outlier: BMO Hold, $580.
META.business: Strong top line, deteriorating cash profile. Q3 revenue $64.6B (+26% YoY, 17th straight sales beat); Q4 guide raised to $73-76B. But GAAP EPS absorbed a $9.9B child-safety legal charge, Q3 capex of $34.9B exceeded operating cash flow, and FCF was -$2.1B vs +$10.6B a year ago.
META.buzz: Heavy buy-the-dip social chatter — Instagram creators list META first among 'stocks to buy on the dip'; Yahoo Finance's Oct 24 'Vibe Check' framed Q3 as green-flag vs red-flag with commenters split on cash flow vs the $135-145B capex plan. Engaged and divided, not euphoric.
META.dip: Spending/margin shock, twice. Q2 (late July): -9% after the capex guide was raised and operating income fell on legal/severance charges. Q3 (Oct 21): revenue beat, but shares fell ~6-7% on Oct 22 amid a Nasdaq AI selloff, as investors focused on negative free cash flow, $825B of future capex/lease commitments, and a new non-voting Class C share plan.
META.risks: FCF stays negative if capex keeps climbing without visible AI monetization; margin compression, Reality Labs losses, and legal exposure still growing.

NFLX.analysts: A downgrade wave. Pre-earnings: Huber Research cut to Underweight ($70); KeyBanc cut its target to $85. Post-earnings: Needham downgraded to Hold; BofA $105->$90, Morgan Stanley $80->$77, Rosenblatt $75->$71; at least 14 brokerages cut targets. Deutsche Bank and UBS stayed constructive ('no new negatives' beyond an ad-rollout delay).
NFLX.business: Profitable and cash-generative but decelerating. Q3 revenue $12.87B (+11.8% YoY — in line, but the slowest growth in nearly three years); EPS $0.87 vs $0.82; net income +43.5%; operating margin 34.6%. Against that: Q4 guide below consensus, the 2026 ad-revenue forecast cut to $2.7B from ~$3B, FCF guide trimmed, ~6% of staff laid off and top content executives replaced days before the report.
NFLX.buzz: Cautious, not a dip-buying chorus — Motley Fool: 'not desperate to add,' would consider buying only below ~19x forward earnings; Zacks steered dip-believers toward ETFs instead of the single stock. Little social dip enthusiasm vs heavy META chatter.
NFLX.dip: Guidance, not the quarter — the second guidance-led drop of the season (shares had already fallen ~11% on Jul 17 on weak Q3 guidance). Q3 reported Oct 20: EPS beat, then the stock fell ~5-6% after Q4 guidance missed and the full-year outlook was cut.
NFLX.risks: The growth-engine story is what's impaired — view-hours grew only ~2% in H1 2026 against YouTube/short-form competition; the ad business is admittedly 'behind our aggressive target'; Q4 margin guided to ~26% on restructuring costs; the next real catalyst is the Q4 report in Jan 2027.

NVDA.analysts: Strong Buy consensus, mean target ~$327 (+55%). Wedbush's Dan Ives reiterated Outperform with a $300 target (Oct 16); Bernstein $400, Rosenblatt $390, Redburn $325, Piper Sandler initiated Overweight $300.
NVDA.business: Fundamentally very strong. Last reported quarter (Aug 26): revenue $96.2B (+106% YoY), data center $89.0B (+117%), gross margin 75%, preliminary FY28 outlook ~70% revenue growth.
NVDA.buzz: The loudest buy-the-dip chorus of the group — Ives explicitly called the selloff 'a buying opportunity'; Motley Fool pitched 'buy in October' at a decade-low valuation (~28x trailing); retail dip-buying content featured entries ~$215.
NVDA.dip: Sector/market-driven, not company-specific: an October AI-wide reassessment — chips fell eight straight sessions on AI-financing and circular-debt fears, reports OpenAI revenue came in below leaked figures, and hot inflation/rate worries (-4%+ on Thu Oct 22 as the SOX fell >6%).
NVDA.risks: If AI-capex financing skepticism deepens (neocloud debt), the multiple compresses further; Meta/Alphabet in-house chips could erode share and pricing power; Street sees gross margin slipping below 72% in Q4 on memory costs.

TMUS.analysts: Moderate Buy consensus, average target ~$242-248 — the widest implied upside of the researched group (~+65%). JPMorgan trimmed to $260 Overweight (Sep 21); Scotiabank $212 Sector Outperform (Oct 9); Raymond James upgraded to Outperform (Oct 12, target $170 — well below peers); Bernstein Neutral, $180 (Oct 21).
TMUS.business: Operationally solid. Q2 service revenue +9% to $19.0B, postpaid service revenue +13%, revenue $22.79B; FY26 guidance reaffirmed in September and adjusted FCF guidance raised to $18.4-18.8B; dividend raised 15% on Sep 24. Q3 due Oct 28.
TMUS.buzz: More fear than dip-buying in tone — coverage is dominated by the SpaceX threat and 'more than two-year low' headlines; retail sentiment on Stocktwits turned bullish, but fewer explicit buy-the-dip features than for BKNG/MCD/CAT.
TMUS.dip: Two company/sector shocks: (1) a sharp drop around Q2 (Jul 23) despite raised FCF guidance, as postpaid net account adds fell 13% YoY with 0.99% churn; (2) SpaceX — the stock fell 13.2% on Oct 9, its worst day since 2013, on SpaceX's ~$8B acquisition of nationwide 800 MHz spectrum, then -7.7% on Oct 23 on reports SpaceX is seeking ~80,000 U.S. cell sites for a wireless build-out. AT&T and Verizon sold off too — sector-wide competitive repricing.
TMUS.risks: The dip driver is potentially structural — a well-capitalized Starlink Mobile entrant could end the three-carrier oligopoly economics. Add slowing subscriber growth, sector read-through risk, and leverage (debt/equity 1.48).
